clue.text: Lacking detail of brief encounter by stretch of water in Norfolk

parts.note: the Norfolk Broads are shallow lakes in eastern England; each is a broad
a brush is a short, fleeting meeting, as in a brush with the law

explanation.surface: Someone recalls only vaguely a fleeting meeting beside a lake in Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England, a holiday boating region.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-brush account paints only in wide strokes, giving the general outline with no fine points.

clue.text: Smashed sculpture

definitions.meaning: broken, as a phone that is ...
a carved or cast head and shoulders portrait

explanation.surface: A statue that has been broken to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust is informal for broken, and also names a sculpted head-and-shoulders likeness.

clue.text: Traditional dolls Choo designed

indicators.note: something designed is laid out afresh, so these letters are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Dolls created by the shoe designer Jimmy Choo are classic in style.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Choo is a fashion shoe designer; 'designed' rearranges DOLLSCHOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-school means conservative and conventional, keeping to established ways.

clue.text: Clean frock

definitions.meaning: to ... a wound is to clean and bind it; to ... a fowl is to clean it for cooking

explanation.surface: A spotless frock, or an instruction to wash one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing a wound or a carcass means cleaning and preparing it; a frock is a garment of that name.

clue.text: Hurry to secure books I dismiss as worthless

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast within, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: to rush is to hurry
BB is an abbreviation for books

explanation.surface: Someone rushing to get hold of some books that they consider worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish something, in British usage, is to criticise it as having no value.

clue.text: Spend lavishly in plant skirting lake

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so the plant wraps around the lake

parts.note: spurge is a plant with milky sap, euphorbia
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Splashing out on plants growing round the edge of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to indulge in extravagant spending.

clue.text: Boss axing one restaurant worker

indicators.note: axing something cuts it out, so the piece for one is removed

parts.note: a chief is a boss or leader
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boss sacking one of the staff at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is the cook in charge of a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Those who have inherited pretentious manners, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase says the word for pretentious manners is spoken and a word sounding the same is written

parts.note: putting on airs means behaving affectedly

explanation.surface: Inheritors putting on pretentious manners, as rich heirs might.
explanation.definitionFit: Heirs are the people who receive an estate or title by inheritance; the clue's phrase describes them.

clue.text: Annual pop celebration?

parts.note: pop looks like music, as in an annual pop festival, but here it means dad, a yearly day honouring him

explanation.surface: A yearly festival of pop music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' suggests pop music; it is a familiar word for a father.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly occasion each June celebrating dads, pop being an affectionate word for a father.

clue.text: Small border plant

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
an edge is a border or boundary

explanation.surface: A little plant for the edge of a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Writer's tip after social function

indicators.note: after places the word for tip behind the word for social function

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
a point is a sharp tip

explanation.surface: An author's advice following a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's tip' reads as an author's advice, but 'Writer' alone is the definition, a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint is a pen, the thing that writes, here treated as a writer.

clue.text: Drama training by new enclosure

parts.note: a play is a drama
PE is physical education, exercise training

explanation.surface: Theatre training held next to a new fenced area.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a small portable fenced area where a young child can play safely.

clue.text: I search out purser

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will hunt down the ship's money officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A purser handles money on a ship, as a bank teller does at a counter; both keep the cash.

clue.text: A key passage

parts.note: a key, as in the Florida Keys, is a low island, so an isle

explanation.surface: An important corridor, or a crucial section of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats or shelves.

clue.text: At hospital, female wearing brooch, attending the German pioneer

indicators.note: the brooch is worn around the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: a pin is a decorative brooch
H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: At a hospital, a woman with a brooch accompanies a German trailblazer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathfinder goes ahead to discover a way, as an explorer or innovator does.

clue.text: Stop a black bull heading off

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, of the word for bull is cut off

parts.note: bull is military slang for excessive cleaning and polishing

explanation.surface: Halting a black bull by heading it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' in British military slang is pointless spit-and-polish, so POLISH; drop its first letter for OLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish something is to put an end to it formally, to do away with it.

clue.text: Extremely earnest in past, perhaps

parts.note: the past is one grammatical tense, so this is an example

explanation.surface: Someone who was very serious in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense describes great seriousness or strong feeling, very earnest in manner.

clue.text: Intimate intercity train

definitions.meaning: a verb here: to put into words, to convey
a fast train making few stops

explanation.surface: A cosy long-distance train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' looks like an adjective, close; it is the verb meaning to make known.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to make known, as to express a view is; an express is a fast train.

clue.text: Observes appropriate military command

parts.note: eyes as a verb means watches or observes
right means proper or appropriate

explanation.surface: Someone keeps watch and issues a fitting order to soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: On parade this order tells troops to turn their heads to the right, often in salute.

clue.text: Case: travelling sort he left inside

indicators.note: inside puts the abbreviation for left within the rearranged letters
travelling suggests letters on the move, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective's case notes: a wandering type, he departed while inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges SORTHE into HOSTER; 'inside' then puts L within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is a leather case for carrying a pistol.

clue.text: Do without chorus

definitions.meaning: to abstain or hold back from something
a repeated section of a song

explanation.surface: Manage without a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to abstain from doing; a refrain is the recurring part of a song.

clue.text: The old lady eating with the Spanish statesman

indicators.note: eating takes the other pieces inside the mother's word

parts.note: the old lady is slang for mother, so ma
and means together with
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A mother dining in company with a Spanish politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old lady' is slang for one's mother, MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela was South Africa's first black president, a celebrated statesman.

clue.text: Pitman with a large soft drink

parts.note: a pitman works down a coal pit, a miner
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A coal worker ordering a big fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In British and Irish usage minerals are carbonated drinks such as lemonade.

clue.text: Dramatist and writer for children almost returned

indicators.note: returned means the shortened name is turned back to front
almost means the last letter of the name is left off

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and other children's books

explanation.surface: A playwright and a children's author nearly came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims NESBIT to NESBI; 'returned' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian author of plays such as A Doll's House.

clue.text: American brought over his cracked Oriental dish

indicators.note: brought over means turned over, so the abbreviation is read backwards
cracked means broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American carried across his broken Oriental plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' turns US into SU; 'cracked' rearranges HIS as SHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese food of vinegared rice with fish or vegetables.

clue.text: Biased against fine amusement park

indicators.note: against means next to, so the word for biased leans on the abbreviation for fine

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
unfair means prejudiced or biased

explanation.surface: Prejudiced against a good amusement park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biased against' reads as one phrase; 'against' only places UNFAIR beside F.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair is a travelling show with rides and stalls, a type of amusement park.

clue.text: Spontaneous remark from daughter in 'Ali Baba', at the start

indicators.note: in places the daughter's letter inside the other letters
at the start picks only the opening letter of the second word

explanation.surface: An improvised line from a girl appearing in a pantomime of Ali Baba.
explanation.walkthrough: Ali Baba is a pantomime staple in Britain, where unscripted lines are common.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad-lib is an unscripted, improvised remark.

clue.text: Box son on equal footing

parts.note: on a par means equal

explanation.surface: A boxing son fights on equal terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container; it is the verb to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice.

clue.text: Duke is to retire in ruin

parts.note: to repair to a place is to go or withdraw there

explanation.surface: A duke is going to withdraw into a ruined state.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is poor condition from neglect, as a building falling into ruin.

clue.text: Bit of help on getting out of bed

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: A little help getting up in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side of the field is also called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A leg-up is a boost or helping hand, literally help climbing onto a horse.

clue.text: To attack king, assistance is required

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: To assault the king, help is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault, and to raid is to attack.

clue.text: Child in joint with unruly tribe

parts.note: the ankle is a joint of the leg

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child with a sore joint among a rowdy clan.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankle-biter is jocular slang for a small child, one at about ankle height.
